reasoning_summary: The statistics are clean. The run completed with max Courant 0.38878. The drag record shows 12 stationary cycles, a mean-drag drift of 0.00018797 and a 95% CI of 5.8758e-05. The inlet is uniform and blockage is 0.0125. None of this shows the answer is converged in space.

The mesh is very coarse for a vortex-shedding problem: 7616 cells over a domain extending 30D upstream, 50D downstream and 40D half-height. The representative cell size is 0.91664 D. The wake has only 56 streamwise cells, and the last wake cell is 2.0173 D. The shed vortices have a period of about 6.4 convective units, so the far wake cannot carry them without heavy numerical damping.

The convection scheme is linearUpwind on this coarse grid, so numerical dissipation in the wake can shift shedding frequency and mean drag. There is only one mesh, with no refinement or second-run comparison. The 3% tolerance on Cd and St is therefore unsupported.

The Strouhal frequency resolution is 0.013333, which is about 8.6% of the reported St of 0.15561. That is well above the 3% tolerance. The FFT value equals the reported value exactly, so it gives no independent check. The 642.64 steps per period give a finer estimate, but it carries the same mesh-resolution risk.

The stationary window starts at 67.598, which is flagged as the MSER cap. It is earlier than the declared averaging start of 75.0, so the transient removal is not clearly confirmed. This is a minor concern next to the mesh issue.

The tight statistical error bars measure only temporal sampling noise on this one mesh. Spatial and numerical-scheme error is unquantified and likely larger than 3% given the 0.92 D representative cell size and the coarse wake. I judge both quantities untrustworthy at the requested tolerance.
